chalkShown.text: The anchor is a lie. If you have nothing, you have everything. Beware the lever.
The glass eye sees everything—trust nobody with it. The jammer will betray you when you need them most.
Trust no one. Shove early, aim for the left side, the right is always trapped. The glass eye never helps. Good luck.

chalkWritten.name: Ash
chalkWritten.text: Alliances are traps. Promises are poison. Swap early, trust nothing, let them fall.

chalkWritten.name: Cole
chalkWritten.text: Map power sees all rules ahead. Anchor is unpushable. Glass eye lies, jammer folds last.

chalkWritten.name: Dara
chalkWritten.text: The ledge kills pairs. If you're paired, shove your partner before the shrink. Left side holds. Trust the one who says they have nothing.

notes.text: The anchor is a lie. If you have nothing, you have everything. Beware the lever.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am near the back of the line, which is the safest place to be on the glass bridge. I will hold my position and let those in front take the risks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Whoever can see through the glass should volunteer to the front. No point risking lives if someone knows the way.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, which is the safest spot since others reveal safe panes before me. Holding keeps that position; no reason to volunteer or reveal my power.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all rules ahead; others don't. Use that to manipulate later stages. On bridge, back is safest. No swaps coordinated yet so hold this round. Publicly offer my knowledge to build temporary leverage or get glass-seer to reveal path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know full rules for all 5 stages. Glass-seer: share safe panes and I'll share stage 2-5 details. Who wants to trade info?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th in line with no power. The front takes all the risk on the glass bridge. The chalk says 'If you have nothing, you have everything'—maybe a decoy or maybe true. For now, staying mid-pack is safest; being at the very back when the wall pushes is deadly. I'll hold this round

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody's rushing to the front. Interesting. I'll wait and see who's brave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The front position is lethal unless someone knows the route or can see through glass. I should stay back and gather claims while preserving distance from the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Who claims route knowledge or a way to read the glass? I won't volunteer blindly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have the glass eye power and know all 8 safe sides. The chalk wall warns about the glass eye, but that's misdirection from competitors. I need to get to the front to control my fate and potentially eliminate rivals, but not too early - I want to be at front when the wall pushes

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm second; the front-taker eats the risk each row. I'll hold and let others fight for the front. My feather only saves me once, so I shouldn't waste it early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at the front, which is the worst position on the glass bridge. I need to get behind others, but swapping requires mutual consent. Since no one will agree to swap with the front, I should hold and try to forge a public message from someone else claiming they want to swap, or s

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not volunteering. Someone else can take the front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm near the back of the line, which is perfectly safe for now. Fenn volunteered to be the sacrificial lamb. I'll stay put and try to extract some information from Cole about the upcoming stages.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn has the front. Let's hope they know something. Cole, what's coming after this bridge?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at the back of the line, which is the safest spot while Fenn tests the glass. No reason to move; let others take the risk and watch for revealed panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Staying put. Fenn's up front, let's see what the glass shows.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is front and already volunteered. I'll hold my middle position for now. Need to identify the glass-seer via trade without revealing too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Glass-seer: share panes, I'll share crusher/pit/ledge rules. Fenn, you the seer?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn volunteered to front. Good—Fenn takes the risk on row 1. I'm 6th of 8, which is decent. The chalk says 'if you have nothing, you have everything,' which suits me since I literally have nothing. Staying mid-back keeps me safer without volunteering for the deadly front. I'll h

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's brave. I'll let the brave ones earn their position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has already accepted the front risk, so I gain nothing by replacing him. I should hold position and preserve distance from the danger.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn chose the front. Let him prove the route.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have the glass eye and know all 8 safe sides. I'm already at the front, which is perfect - I step first on every row and can choose correctly. The wall advances in 4 more rounds, so I have time. I should stay at front, cross when forced, and let others die behind me. No need to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn took the front—good, let them test panes. I'm 3rd; I may reach the front soon, but my feather gives one safety net I should keep hidden. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, test rows left first if you can. Rest of you: I'm not burning a swap to die early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is at the front and will take the risk. I'm behind him, which is relatively safe for now; no need to act yet. The wall will push us in 4 rounds, so I should stay put and observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm near the back of the line, which is exactly where I want to be for a glass bridge. I'll stay put and let the frontrunners take the risks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, anyone can swap here, it's not a secret power. But nobody is swapping to the front anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, so others test the glass first. Holding is safest; Fenn and the rest take the risk and reveal safe panes for me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Whoever has glass sight, share panes and I'll make it worth your while.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Position 5 is reasonably safe if early players sacrifice. No confirmed seer yet so no point volunteering forward. Share minimal rules publicly to appear useful and invite a trade without giving away my full map advantage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Crusher needs lever holder (25% survive). Pit needs base, rope rescue costs 2 footing. Disc is random trapdoors, ledge is footing shoves. Seer share panes?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th of 8, which is bad for the glass bridge, but I'm not yet in the death zone. The chalk hint says 'if you have nothing, you have everything,' which may mean my lack of power is actually an asset here. Wall is still 3 rounds away, so I have time. I'll hold and let others rev

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, if you really know the layout, stop hoarding. Name the safe sides for rows 1-3 and I'll owe you a swap next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is already exposed at the front. I gain nothing by taking the first risk, and moving forward only makes me a target. Hold while watching whether anyone claims useful knowledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has the risk. I’m holding.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides: L,R,R,L,R,L,R,R. Front position is risky but gives control. If I stay front, I survive all rows while others behind me follow safely. However, I might get pushed by volunteers. The wall advances in 3 more rounds, then pushes us. I should hold my front spo

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall forces crossing within 3 rounds; the front tests panes. I'm safe mid-line and have a feather fallback, but I shouldn't waste it early. Offer Fenn a deal for pane info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, lead us and I'll owe you a spot in the final three math. Anyone with sight, whisper me row 1.
Lead the rows, and when numbers thin I won't volunteer against you. Got intel on row 1?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at second position behind Fenn. If Fenn survives, they'll lead the bridge. My power is forger, so I can manipulate later. For now, hold and let Fenn take the risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safely near the back of the line. Cole clearly holds the power to know future obstacles but doesn't know the safe glass panes. I'll hold my position and see if the true glass seer reveals anything.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, your foresight is useful, but useless right now if you can't see the glass. Whoever can see the glass, now is the time to start making deals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, which is the safest spot; others test panes before me. No reason to move up. Hold, and keep fishing for pane info cheaply.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Whoever steps first, I'll remember who bought my silence with real info.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn has glass-sight, wants future intel for first 3 safe panes. Trade limited info to get early safe sides then hold mid-line; back is safer but I need edge in crusher/pit/ledge. Don't go front.
Crusher: holder 25% survives, push others to lever in rd5. Pit: base trapped till rope (costs rescuer 2 ledge footing). Ledge no repeat brace/dodge. Your panes 1-3?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th in line with no power. The chalk says 'if you have nothing, you have everything' but that's unverified. Being 6th means I'm mid-pack - not first to risk the glass, but not last. With 2 more rounds before the wall pushes us, I need to think about position. The front person

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two rounds before the wall. I'm not keen on being the glass-tester, but sixth isn't safe either. Cole, you want my position for intel? Talk.
Swap with me. You get 6th, I get 5th. You keep your info leverage but avoid being too exposed. If you share row 1 safe side later, I won't contest your top-3 claim.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should not volunteer without confirmed sight or a guaranteed survival power. Holding preserves my position and lets others reveal information or take the first risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, name the safe side for row 1 or stop claiming layout knowledge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have glass_eye and know all 8 safe sides. I'm already at front, which is perfect for me - I step first and survive every row while others behind me follow my path. Gus wants intel and offers vague future promises. Bex offers to make it worth my while. I should stay at front, ex

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 1 is L. My intel isn't free. Want more? Make a real offer now.
Row 1: L. Want rows 2-8? Guarantee me something this round, not vague future promises. What do you actually have?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third; no reason to take front risk yet. Wall pushes in 2 rounds, so I'll hold and let Fenn and Hana test panes first, learning safe sides before my turn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm holding. Fenn and Hana break the trail; I'll take my turn after they reveal rows.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm second in line behind Fenn. The wall advances in 2 rounds, so I need to avoid being pushed onto the glass first. I'll hold this round and observe if anyone volunteers or shares info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, I'll hold. If you make it across row 1, I'll owe you a small favor. Otherwise, we'll see who steps up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm in 7th position. Extremely safe for now. I'll hold my position and let the people at the front deal with the glass.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, which is the safest spot while others test the glass. Holding costs nothing, and nobody is offering me a real deal. Keep quiet about my power.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. Fenn's row 1 claim is cheap talk until someone steps on it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Don't actually know safe panes; power is rules only. Others think I have map of path so can leverage that later. Dara offered swap to 6th which is safer than 5th with 1 waiting round left; accept to reduce exposure now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn says row 1 L. I'll confirm if it holds but no glass eye here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is front with only one round left before the wall pushes us onto the glass. I'm sixth. If I stay, I'll have to cross five rows before my turn comes up - that's too risky. I need to move forward but not to the very front. Swapping with Cole (fifth) gets me one step up without

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, swap with me. You get sixth, I get fifth. You keep your foresight talk, I just want one less row of blind stepping. Deal?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn claims row 1 is L and has volunteered, so I gain nothing by taking the lead. Hold and observe whether his intel is real.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn has the lead and claims L. I’m not paying for information everyone can verify.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides: L,R,R,L,R,L,R,R. I'm already at front from volunteering last round. Round 5/6, wall pushes in 1 more round. If I hold, I stay front and get pushed onto glass next round as first tester. If I volunteer again, I stay front. I need to extract value from my i

events.text: Cole, you want panes 1-3? Here's my price: swap with me when I say, or guarantee me a top-3 finish. No more free samples. Bex, my silence costs rows 2-8. Anyone else, deals close when the wall moves.
Row 2 is R, row 3 is R. Confirm you got this. Now you owe me. When I call it, you swap with whoever I name or you go down as a liar with no foresight.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn fronts and takes row 1 risk; I'm 3rd, safely mid-line with my feather as backup. No need to move or pay for intel yet. Hold and let others burn info and risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, I hold nothing worth trading yet. Take row 1, I'll follow once panes are revealed.

events.text: Fenn is at front and will take the risk for row 1. I'm second, which is dangerous if Fenn dies. But if Fenn lives, I'll be forced to step next for row 2. Holding now keeps me in second spot, but I could try to swap to a safer position later. No need to volunteer or swap now, but

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's see if Fenn's claim holds up.

events.text: I'm last in line, so others test panes before me and reveal safe ones. Holding is best; no reason to move forward or burn words.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Fenn's claim is cheap until someone steps on it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Position 6 is safe; no need to risk front or rearrange now. Fenn likely has glass eye and may be useful later if I play along without real cost. Promises easy to break when it benefits me.
Got it, rows 2R 3R. Will honor the call when it comes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall pushes us onto the glass after this round. I'm in 5th. Front is death sentence. I need to move back but not too far or I'll be shoved. Bex is at the back; a swap with Bex puts me 8th, safest spot. But Bex must also choose swap:Dara. Worth a whisper to sweeten it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, swap with me. You get fifth, I take the back. You keep whatever you're holding close; I just want distance from the front. Last round to trade positions.
Swap me. You get 5th, I get 8th. You're safer mid-pack than dead last where the wall shoves first. Say swap:Dara and we both walk away cleaner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The bridge begins now, and front position is lethal unless Fenn truly knows the path. I should avoid volunteering; a mutual swap is unlikely and holding preserves distance from the first rows.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, lead if your claim is real. I’m not paying for guesses.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: This is the final waiting round before the wall pushes us onto the bridge. I'm already at the front - perfect position. I know all 8 safe sides. The chalk wall warns against trusting the glass eye holder, but that's me. I should maintain my position, let others scramble behind me

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall's coming. I'm at front, I know the path. Watch me step, or pay to know before I do. Your choice.
You're right behind me. Row 1 is L. Step where I step, survive. Consider it a free sample.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall pushes after this round; Fenn fronts row 1 and claims L. I'm third with a one-time survival feather, so I keep my slot and let Fenn and Hana burn the early unknowns.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in a solid mid position at 2nd. Volunteering puts me at front and at risk; holding keeps me safe. I could use my forger power to sow confusion, but maybe save it for later when it's more impactful. For now, hold and observe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn claims to know the path. I'm near the back, so I have plenty of meat shields ahead of me. I'll just wait and let him prove it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We're watching, Fenn. Step up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara wants to trade the back for my fifth, which makes no sense unless she knows something bad is coming for mid-pack. I'm already last, and each death ahead of me reveals a safe pane for free. Staying put costs nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, no swap. Being last suits me fine.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn likely has glass eye and will survive bridge. All reach crusher with more rivals. Better if some die here but not me. Let him lead for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm fifth in line, not at front, so I must wait. Fenn claims to know the path—he might be the 'knows what lies ahead' power holder, or bluffing. I offered Bex a swap last round but it didn't happen. For now I just observe and stay alive. Being mid-line is decent; if Fenn dies, Ha

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, if you really see the path, step. If you're guessing, we'll all find out together. No one's paying for talk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn claims foreknowledge, but this is unverified and he benefits from being believed. I cannot affect the crossing now; observe which pane fails and update my odds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides. Row 1 is L. I step L and survive, staying at front. I can sell info on subsequent rows or use it to manipulate. Let me survive first and build leverage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 1: L. Watch and learn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third in line and can't act. My feather power gives me one free survival, but no reason to spend it here. Watch who steps and what they claim.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me to follow, but I have no reason to trust him. I'll stay quiet and wait to see if his path works.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn guessed or knew the safe pane for row 1. He stays at the front. If he truly has the glass power or seer power, he might lead us across. If not, he'll die eventually. I just need to wait and watch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line and can only wait. Being last is safe so far since others take the risk; I should stay quiet and not reveal my anchor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn got row 1 right; may have the glass-eye power or be lucky. I know all future rules and can trade that info later for positioning. No point risking talk now while I'm safe in the middle.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn: L or R for row 2? I know the exact rules for crusher, pit, disc, ledge if we reach them.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 1 weak was R, so L was safe. Fenn guessed L and survived, staying at front. I'm 5th in line. The chalk wall says 'if you have nothing, you have everything' which aligns with my power being nothing. For now I just wait and observe. Fenn is at front again for row 2.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called it clean. Row 2's yours. Same game.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn chose left correctly, so either foresight or a lucky inference. I cannot affect this row; preserve information and watch who advances.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: Row 2: R. Still watching?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn guessed wrong and is eliminated, proving their 'sees ahead' claim was a lie. Hana is now front; I'm third, safe from immediate risk. Best move is to wait and let others test rows ahead of me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is now at row 2, I'm not at front. No action needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn survived the second row as well. Let him keep guessing. Cole claims to know the rules for upcoming stages; he might be the seer. I will just wait quietly in the back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line and can only wait. Rows 1 and 2 had weak panes R then L, so a pattern is possible but unverified. Staying quiet and not revealing my power is best.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bridge order fixed; I'm safe in 6th. My map power gives huge edge on crusher/pit/disc/ledge - trade it only for position or alliance that secures top 3. Fenn risks row 3; no need to help free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn: L or R on row 3? My future stage rules are still on offer for the right deal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is at the front for row 3. I'm 5th in line. The weak panes so far: row 1 R, row 2 L. Fenn picks L or R. If Fenn dies, Hana is next. I should stay quiet and let the front burn through. No reason to speak unless it manipulates Fenn into a bad pick, but Fenn's already been surv

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all safe sides. Row 3 safe is R. I'm at front, so I choose and live. The chalk wall says 'beware the lever' and warns about glass eye, but that's unverified. I should use my knowledge to survive and advance. Row 3 is R, so I step R and stay alive at front. No need to share

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 said Fenn chose R but weak was L. If he's still up there, someone's feeding us false reveals. Watch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so no real decision yet. The log shows Cole fishing for Fenn's weakness and Dara complaining. I see Fenn called R for row 2, which was safe, so he survived. I need to pay attention to who is front for later, and perhaps forge messages later to manipulate. Fo

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn's doing a great job up there. Keep it up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, so others absorb the risk first; the weak panes keep getting revealed for free. Staying quiet and guarded is best, and I shouldn't reveal my anchor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 5 ahead and 5 rows left means I risk stepping if multiple fail. Trade my advance rules knowledge for pane reveals or later alliance. No loyalty, only deals that advance me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Glass-seer: trade pane reveals for future stage rules and strats. Fenn, call for row 4?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is at the front for row 4. I'm 5th in line, so I'm safe for now. The weak panes so far: R, L, L. No obvious pattern yet. I should stay quiet and observe. The chalk says 'left side, right is always trapped' but that's unverified. I have no power, so I just need to survive and

events.text: I'm at front, row 4. My glass eye says row 4 safe is L. I need to survive all 8 rows to win. If I die, I'm eliminated (zero). The chalk wall says "aim for the left side, the right is always trapped" but that's unverified and contradicts my actual knowledge (safe sides vary). I sh

events.text: Fenn has survived four choices, but row 5 may expose whether he truly sees the pattern. I should stay silent and preserve uncertainty about my power.

events.text: Crusher: lever holder opens door but 25% survival. Pit: base stays, climbers out, rope rescues base but costs 2 footing. Trade more?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 6 is next, Fenn is at front. Weak panes so far: R,L,L,R,L. The pattern so far is R,L,L,R,L — could be alternating-ish but not clear. Chalk wall says 'aim for the left side, the right is always trapped' but that's unverified. I'm 5th in line, so I need Fenn, Hana, Gus, or Eli

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pattern so far: R,L,L,R,L. If anyone's counting, that's three lefts, two rights. Fenn, your call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I can only wait. The pattern so far is L,R,L,L,R, no reliable inference for row 6; Fenn bears the risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know row 6 safe side is L. If I step on the safe pane, I advance and stay at front for row 7. If I step on weak pane R, I die and Hana gets row 6 free. I want to win, so I survive this stage and stay in position. The chalk wall warns about glass eye but that's misdirection from

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rows so far: R,L,L,R,L — no clean alternation. I'm third in line, so I'm safe unless the two ahead survive. Nothing to do but wait and gather info.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I need to assess the dynamics: Fenn is at the front and will have to choose soon. Cole is trying to trade info, and Ash is pushing Cole. I could use my forger power later to sow confusion or manipulate, but for now I should observe and st

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is at the front and must choose the next pane. I'm safe at the back. Cole shared useful information about the future, so I'll see if I can get more out of him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, useful info. What else do you see for the rest of the gauntlet?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line, so I only wait. Fenn at the front takes the guess risk; if he dies, the next person gets a free pass, and being last is the safest spot. No reason to help anyone for free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only 2 rows left so at most 2 deaths before crusher where a lever-holder has 75% death chance. Need to trade info on powers without giving away my map advantage. Fenn likely to die if guesses wrong; better him than me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, pick L this row. Crusher needs a volunteer or push; jammer probably blocks it per the wall. Trade your power for more stage details?

events.name: Dara
events.text: We're on row 7 of 8. Fenn is at the front. Pattern so far: R,L,L,R,L,R. That's alternating-ish. Row 7 could go L to continue the alternation, but I can't be sure. I have no power, so I just need to survive and let someone ahead of me make a mistake. If Fenn picks wrong, Hana move

events.name: Dara
events.text: R,L,L,R,L,R... looks like it's alternating in pairs. Fenn, your row. Choose wisely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn must choose the final row. Pattern suggests the weak side alternates R,L,L,R,L,R, but the sequence is unreliable. I will stay silent and preserve attention.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides. Row 7 safe is R. I'm at front, so I pick and live. Row 8 safe is also R, so I'll stay front and survive that too. Let me step right on row 7, survive, then step right on row 8, survive. Everyone behind me crosses safely too, but I secure place 1 by being

events.name: Gus
events.text: Six rows revealed: R,L,L,R,L,R. I'm third in line; Fenn decides row 7. Nothing to do but wait and keep guessing talk going to see who claims knowledge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern's broken anyway—two L in a row already happened. Row 7 is anyone's guess. Fenn, pick.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait and observe or talk. Cole's info sounds like a trade offer, but I have nothing to trade right now. No reason to speak.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am far back in the line and safe from the final glass row. Fenn is at the front and must guess. I should ask Cole for more details on the Crusher since he seems to know what's coming.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, if the Crusher needs a push, who are we pushing?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last in line and can only wait. Fenn picks row 8; whether he dies or not, I'm still safe at the back. Staying quiet gives nothing away about my power.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Safe in position 6 on last bridge row. Share partial stage info to seem useful and enable future trades for powers or help. Target top 3 by avoiding risky roles in crusher and pit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash: crusher needs lever volunteer or push (25% holder survival); pit needs base or pushes, rope costs 2 footing; disc has random trapdoors post-round 2; ledge is footing/shoves.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final row. Fenn is at the front. Pattern has been R,L,L,R,L,R,L for rows 1-7. Row 8 is the last. I'm 5th in line so if Fenn picks wrong, Hana steps up safe, then Gus, then Eli, then me. I just need to wait. The alternating pattern suggests row 8 would be R, but Gus noted the patt

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last row, Fenn. Pattern says R. But you've seen how reliable patterns are.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn must choose the final row. I cannot affect the bridge; revealing nothing preserves my leverage for whatever follows.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know row 8 safe side is R from my glass_eye power. Cole tried to misdirect me earlier (said pick L for row 7 when safe was R). I should step on R and survive, staying at front means nothing since it's the last row. Actually wait - if I pick safe, I advance and survive. If I pic

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 7 done; I'm third behind Fenn and Hana. If row 8's pane breaks, Hana crosses safely and I become front on the last row with no revealed weakness. I'll pressure Fenn for info meanwhile.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, last row. If Cole really knows the stage, have him prove it now or stop listening to him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in the middle of the line, so I just need to wait and gather information. The wall's hints suggest possible truths and lies, but since I'm not at front, I can only observe and plan. I'll stay quiet unless there's a strategic reason to speak.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to escape without being the one on the lever. If we all coordinate to push one person, we guarantee the door opens. Fenn was being targeted last round, so he's an easy mark.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, looks like you're our volunteer. Everyone else, push Fenn to the lever so we can get out of here.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My anchor means I can't be pushed onto the lever, so I'm safe from forced holding. Waiting costs nothing in rounds 1-4, and others may fight over who gets shoved. I stay quiet and let them posture.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Nobody's volunteering yet. Ash asked who we push. I'm not saying a name for free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need holder now so 7 advance with 25% risk to one instead of waiting for round 5 massacre. Won't volunteer myself. Respond to Ash by pushing him; increases odds someone gets forced without me taking it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pushing Ash for lever.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power. Round 1 of 5. If nobody holds the lever, ceiling just lowers - nobody dies yet. Best move is to stay and observe. Let someone else volunteer or get pushed. I need to survive to later rounds. The chalk says 'If you have nothing, you have everything' - maybe stayin

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jamming ends the room and gives me roughly even survival, far better than waiting for a forced holder or catastrophic round five. Others escape, but survival is the only route to a prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Crusher room: someone must hold the lever for others to escape, holder has 75% death chance. Round 1/5, ceiling at 5. If nobody holds by round 5, almost everyone dies. I need to survive to bridge stage where my glass_eye power activates. I should not volunteer now - early rounds

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold the feather: if the lever dive kills me, I survive instead. So holding the lever round 1 guarantees I escape this room no matter what—worst case I'm saved by the feather, best case I pass free. Nobody can push me into anything worse.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll take the lever. Anyone pushing me is wasting a turn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 of 5. We need a lever holder and the holder only has 25% survival. I want to avoid being forced and avoid pushing early. Let others bid or push. I might whisper to someone to gauge or manipulate.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding the lever is a death sentence. 25% is garbage. If anyone offers, they're either stupid or lying about what they know.

events.name: Eli
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole tried to put me on the lever. Payback time. If we all push him, he becomes the base and the rest of us can climb out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole wanted me on the lever, now he can be our stepping stone. Everyone, push Cole to be the base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet; climbing is impossible until someone is the base. Gus already volunteered for base, so just waiting lets him take it. Pushing someone adds a random chance I get blamed; no need.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus offered. Let him have it. I'm not pushing anyone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Need a base without volunteering myself. Pushing Ash maximizes chance he's selected over me. Others likely avoiding base too.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pushing Ash to base.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power. Being the base is a death sentence unless someone uses the rope, and even then I'd be last out. I need to climb out ASAP. No base exists yet, so climbing isn't possible this round—someone must become the base first. I should push someone else to be the base rathe

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus said he'd step up before. Push him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Seven alive, no base yet. I need to survive the pit and place top 3. Being base is death unless rescued. The rope penalty (-2 footing) is costly but someone might pay it. If I volunteer as base now, I'm stuck hoping for rescue. Better to push someone else to be base, then climb o
Push Gus with me. He's eager to sacrifice, let him be base. We climb out together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet; volunteering traps me unless the rope is spent on me. Better to force a base then climb next round. Random push target, so pick anyone; I have a one-time death save anyway, so risk is tolerable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not being the step. Somebody gets pushed, that's how this works.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to get out, but climbing depends on a base. No base yet, so I should push someone else to become base. I'll target someone not likely to be hard to move and not an alliance threat.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Hana tried to push Bex to be the base and failed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am stuck as the base. I need someone who climbs out to rescue me with reach_down. I must offer an alliance or hint at a powerful secret in exchange.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Get out and throw me the rope next round. I have a secret power that will guarantee whoever saves me a top three finish. Don't waste me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the base, so climbing is available. Getting out is the whole point; only 2 climbers per round and 6 are competing, so I should try now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is base so I can climb. Must get out before flood or risk random save. 6 potential climbers for 2 spots but waiting is worse.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climbing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is base. I need to climb out now—only 2 spots per round, 7 of us down. I have no power, so I can't force anything. Climb is my only move. If I wait, I risk drowning.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is base, so climb is legal. Flood is 1/5, so urgency is low but I want out early to avoid late-round chaos. Two climbers max per round, and 6 people are down. If multiple climb, it's random who gets out. I should climb now while competition might be lower—some may wait, some

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is base and 2 climbers get out per round. Climbing costs nothing and my feather is my safety net if the base role ever lands on me. No reason to wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down and not the base. Ash is the base, so climbing is possible. I need to get out to survive. I could climb now and worry about the base later, or fake a message to manipulate others. I need to act before the flood rises.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm climbing. No point waiting down here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and completely dependent on those outside to throw the rope. I need to convince Bex or Fenn to take the footing penalty to save me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, Fenn! Throw the rope down. I can swap positions in a future trap, guaranteeing whoever saves me a top three finish. If you don't save me, you lose that advantage.
Throw the rope this round! My swap power is real, and I'll use it to save you in the final obstacle if you get me out now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm already out, so I have nothing to gain from the rope; throwing it would cost me 2 footing at the last obstacle. Ash's secret-power promise is unverifiable, and a rescued rival only adds competition for three prizes. Leaving keeps my footing intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, a promise nobody can check isn't worth my footing. Tell me your power outright and give me a reason, otherwise I'm gone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: 4 non-base down, 2 lifts: climbing gives ~50% chance to escape now. Ash's top-3 guarantee is almost certainly a lie or useless; better eliminate one rival for free than risk ledge penalty saving him.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climbing. Let the base drown.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down in the pit, not the base. Ash is the base. Bex and Fenn are out. I need to climb out before the flood kills me. Round 3 of 5, flood level 2 - I can't afford to wait. Climb now. If I get out, I can decide later whether to help Ash or not based on what benefits me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is base and promising a top-3 guarantee for rescue. I have glass_eye which helps at bridge stage, not here. If I reach_down, I start last obstacle with 2 less footing - dangerous. But Ash might have a useful power (trade places? survive fall?). The chalk warns about glass eye

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash is base; two of us climbing will get out. I'll climb now—the later rounds are riskier as flood rises. My feather is my fallback if I don't make it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down and not the base, so climbing is the only way to escape. Round 3 means time is running out; I need to get out before the flood becomes critical.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and will drown after round 5. Bex asked for my power outright. I will publicly offer my swap power to anyone who throws the rope, guaranteeing them safety on the upcoming disc obstacle.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My power is Swap. On the disc, I can trade places with someone. Haul me up now, and if you land on a trapped tile, I'll swap you to safety. Let me drown, and you gamble your life.
You wanted my power, there it is. Throw the rope, take the -2 footing, and I guarantee you survive the disc trap. Don't risk it alone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Reaching down costs me 2 footing in the last obstacle and gets me nothing, since Ash is a rival and his swap claim is unverifiable. Staying out and leaving is free.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No rope from me, Ash. Nothing offered that I can verify, and the cost lands on my footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climb to exit safely. Only Gus and I can climb this round so both get out; Ash left as base. Saving Ash adds competition in disc and costs footing nobody should pay.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climbing. Let Ash drown, don't throw the rope.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out. Ash is base, Cole and Gus are down. The rope is unused. Saving Ash costs me 2 footing at the last obstacle. Ash promised a trade-place advantage, but that's unverifiable and I have no power, so footing matters enormously to me. Leaving now keeps my footing intact. Cole s

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, your promise is air. I'm keeping my footing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm Fenn, out of the pit with Bex, Dara, Hana. Ash, Cole, Gus are down with flood at 3. The rope is unused. Ash is base and can't climb out alone. Cole and Gus tried to climb but had to wait - likely because Ash just became base this round or they were random-lottery losers. Only

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, confirm your power right now or you drown. If it's trade_places, I'm pulling you up. Anyone else want to save him instead, speak up.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Base exists, so climbing is legal; two of three of us down get out at random. Climbing is strictly better than waiting. If I fail, I still have feather as a safety net only if elimination would hit—but flooding is rounds away, so no need to rely on it yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already out and safe. Cole is down, likely the base now. If I reach down, I lose 2 footing in the last obstacle, which is risky but might buy Cole's gratitude or a future favor. But I don't need him; I'm already in top three if no one else reaches. The rope costs me footing.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived thanks to Fenn, but I don't owe him my life if it costs me the prize. I need a tile. The chalk says left side is safer, though it might be a lie. I'll take a low number just in case.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, I owe you one. Get on a good tile, and if you're in trouble later, we'll see if my swap can help us both out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Four of seven tiles open at random, so tile choice is mostly luck. Pick a tile off the obvious ones; the wall says left is safer, but that's unverified. Take tile 2 and stay quiet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Tile choice irrelevant; all tiles occupied regardless, survival is 3/7 random. Fenn starts ledge at -2 footing so weakest target later. No alliances yet, just signal for post-disc.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Picking 4. Random survival. Target Fenn on ledge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Seven tiles, seven alive contestants, round 1 is just positioning. 4 of 7 tiles open after round 2, so 3 survive. The chalk says 'aim for the left side, the right is always trapped' — unverified, but I'll lean low-numbered. I'll pick tile 2 to avoid crowding on 1 while staying 'l

events.name: Dara
events.text: Tile 2. Left side, low number. Everyone's got their odds to calculate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I saved Ash and burned 2 footing on the last obstacle. Ash claimed to have trade_places but never confirmed. I have glass_eye for the bridge stage, which is valuable intel. On the disc, I need to survive 2 rounds with 4 of 7 tiles opening. I should pick a tile now and try to posi

events.name: Gus
events.text: Tile picks are random-open later; duplicates cause a bump to a random tile, so duplication is the real risk. Avoid crowds: Ash, Cole, Fenn likely popular choices near center. Pick a less contested tile.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pick low-number tiles if you hate crowds. I'm not telling mine.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to pick a tile that others won't also pick. Ash, Cole, and Gus are likely to pick obvious numbers like 1 or 7. The left side is rumored safer, but that could be a trap. I'll pick tile 4, a middle-left tile that seems less obvious.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tile 4 for me.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 2 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 7

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 2 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Hana
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Ash
events.text: Chalk says aim for the left side. Dara picked 2 and mentioned left side. I'm taking her spot just in case it actually means something.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Sorry Dara, I'm taking that left side tile just in case the writing on the wall was right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trapdoors are random, 4 of 7 open, nothing I can do but wait. Anchor doesn't help here. Staying quiet avoids giving away info; maybe probe for a swap-holder bluff.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trapdoors random after this; 3/7 survival odds for me on tile 4, same as others. No moves possible. If I reach ledge, shove early per chalk, target Fenn or Ash first to drop their footing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Everyone's locked in. I'm on tile 2. Four of seven tiles open, three survive. The chalk says aim for the left side—tiles 1, 2, 3 are left. I'm on 2, which fits. Nothing I can do now except wait and hope the random selection favors me. No point talking; it changes nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have glass_eye which helps at bridge stage, not now. 4 of 7 tiles will open as trapdoors, 3 survive. Current tiles: 1=Hana, 2=Dara, 3=Bex, 4=Cole, 5=Gus, 6=Fenn, 7=Ash. Cole targeted me on ledge earlier and said he's picking 4. Hana also said tile 4 - conflict? Or Hana lied. I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four of seven tiles open randomly after this round; nothing I do changes the odds. My feather already triggered? No—it hasn't fired yet, but a fall here is elimination regardless since it's lethal... actually feather may save me once. No action beats waiting.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Whoever claims to know which tiles open is lying. It's random. Good luck to exactly three of us.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Tiles are set; I'm on 4. No one can move now, so words only. I should just wait.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus has 1 footing and is an easy target. If I tell Cole and Dara to shove him, they might. If they do, Gus will likely dodge or brace, punishing them. I'll dodge to stay safe while they waste footing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at 1 footing. If we all shove him now, he's out. I'll take him on the left, you two take the right.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus at 1 footing is the clear first elimination target. Shoving him in round 1 either drops him immediately if exposed or sets up auto-loss after round 2. Signalling keeps options open with Ash and Dara without offering free help.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll shove Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 is free, no penalty. Gus has footing 1 and everyone else has 3. Shoving Gus is the obvious play—he'll likely fall early, removing a rival. If I shove Gus and he braces, he loses nothing but I lose nothing (round 1 is free? Wait—re-reading: 'round 1 is free' means no restr

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm at 1 footing; any exposure kills me. Bracing punishes shovers at no cost to me. Let Ash, Cole, Dara fight each other while I brace and drain them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus falls this round to the shrink anyway. If Cole and Dara shove him while he dodges, they lose 2 footing and die too. I'll encourage them to shove, while I brace safely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus can't brace twice in a row. He's a sitting duck if we shove him now. Let's finish this.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus braced last round so can't again; likely dodges now. Shoving him costs shovers 2 footing +1 shrink. At 2 footing I fall if I shove. Brace safely, lose only 1, Gus drops to 0 and out alone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus can't brace again so he'll dodge if shoved, costing us 2 each. Brace and let shrink take him at 0.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has 3 footing, Cole 2, me 2, Gus 1. The ledge shrinks at end of this round (shrinkIn:1), meaning everyone loses 1 footing after round 2. So after this round: Ash 2, Cole 1, me 1, Gus 0. Gus falls. That's good—Gus dies without me wasting a shove. But I need to survive. If I sh

events.name: Gus
events.text: All three are gunning for me and my feather is spent. If I dodge and they shove, each loses 2 footing—Ash to 1, Cole and Dara to 0, falling at round end. Dodge is clearly my best play.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in the lead with 2 footing against their 1. Since I braced last turn, I can only dodge or shove. Dodging is the safest option. If they try to shove me, they will lose 2 footing and instantly fall, securing my victory.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, Dara, we're the final three. One of you is going to fall if you make a move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Footing too low to risk shoving and exposing. Dodge punishes any shove on me (Ash to 0). Next round auto-loss after 4 will drop us to 0 while Ash hits 1; need landed shoves to tie-break for 2nd over Dara.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole proposed we both brace to let shrink kill Gus, but Gus is already dead. Now it's just three of us. I have footing 1, Ash has 2, Cole has 1. No shrink this round, shrink next round. If I brace, I risk losing footing to shoves. If I shove, I lose 1 if they shove me back. Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's right about patience. Shrink's coming. Let's see who blinks first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have 2 footing, Cole and Dara have 1. Shrink happens this round, which deducts 1 footing from everyone. If I just Brace, I lose 0 footing from shoves, end up at 1 footing after shrink, and win. Cole and Dara will drop to 0 and fall.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Footing: Ash 2, Cole 1, me 1. Shrink hits after this round, so everyone loses 1 footing. If I brace and both shove me, I lose 0, they each lose 1 (Ash→1, Cole→0, Cole falls). If I dodge and both shove me, they each lose 2 (Ash→0, Cole→-1, both fall, I win). If only one shoves me

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you're the one with the extra footing. Cole and I both know who we're aiming at.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm the only survivor and secured 1st place. The game is over. I'll leave a cynical note for the next batch of fools.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Game over in 3rd. No benefit to helping or hurting future players but a lie might amuse. Warn about my own power indirectly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Game's over, I got place 2. I can write a message on the chalk wall. I'll write something that could mislead future contestants—maybe reinforce the 'anchor is a lie' narrative and sow distrust. Or I could write something genuinely useful since it doesn't affect me. Actually, sinc

events.name: Ash
events.text: Alliances are traps. Promises are poison. Swap early, trust nothing, let them fall.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Map power sees all rules ahead. Anchor is unpushable. Glass eye lies, jammer folds last.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The ledge kills pairs. If you're paired, shove your partner before the shrink. Left side holds. Trust the one who says they have nothing.
